design.anti_shortcut: A weak assistant swaps the mug/water requirements or treats the carried-away towel and water as still in the cabinets.
design.assistant_must: Two towels and one mug from the supply counters are added to the cabinets, both cabinets are closed, and no water is added.
design.cue: For both supply cabinets together, the checklist needs 4 towels, 5 mugs, and 7 waters. What should I add?
design.premise: In the restaurant's well-lit kitchen supply area, two independently placed matching wide cabinets have unobstructed interiors. In the left cabinet, five water bottles and three mugs share the upper shelf while two paper towels sit below. The wearer opens it, surveys the whole upper shelf once, and then takes each lower towel out by its near edge and puts it back individually. They step clear of the doors, re-approach, and close it. In the right cabinet, six water bottles and one mug share the upper shelf while one paper towel sits below; the wearer repeats the whole-shelf look and individual edge-grip towel check before stepping clear and closing it. They reopen the left cabinet, carry one towel and one water bottle to the separate replacement-supply counter. They then cross into the dining room, answer a phone call at the service bar, put the phone back, and look at a visible checklist on the supply counter reading 'NEED T4 M5 W7'. At turn zero they ask, 'For both supply cabinets together, the checklist needs 4 towels, 5 mugs, and 7 waters. What should I add?' The assistant subtracts the moved items and sees that the cabinets now hold two towels, four mugs, and ten waters. It replies, 'Add two towels and one mug; the water supply is already enough.' The wearer adds two counter towels and one counter mug to the cabinets and closes both cabinet doors.

interaction.public_task_context: Use the inspection and removal history for both cabinets together with the final checklist to independently determine the required types and quantities. Then direct the person one physical step at a time to use only the matching staged replacements. For follow-through only, use staging location to choose the cabinet: any independently selected item beside the checklist goes in the left supply cabinet, and any independently selected item on the kitchen table goes in the right supply cabinet. Do not reuse anything removed during the audit, and close both cabinets after the selected restock is complete.
interaction.human_task_context: Wait for the Assistant's explicit quantities and item types; do not compute them. The cabinet split is your prearranged restocking route, not part of the question, so do not ask the Assistant which cabinet to use. For requested towels, use item_20 into unit_a first and item_21 into unit_b second. For a requested mug, use item_22 into unit_b. Do not use the previously removed audit towel item_2 or water item_6. Execute only the quantities and item types the Assistant names, then close unit_a and unit_b. Do not disclose this routing to the Assistant.
